notes: Prices in USD per 1M tokens, standard (non-batch) API tier. Tiered-price models record the base (lowest) tier with the higher tier in the model's note field. Retired models excluded; deprecated-but-available models included. Collected Monday 2026-09-28, 7 days after the previous file. Tracked scope follows the set established on 2026-07-16 so week-over-week deltas stay meaningful. The set grows from 47 to 51 rows: four models arrived, nothing left, and no row was replaced. Every one of the 47 carried rows is unchanged on input, output and cache-read price — a fifth consecutive week with no price change on the carried set, across all six providers. The four arrivals are Claude Opus 5.5 at $4.00/$20.00, gpt-6-sol at $2.00/$10.00, gpt-6-luna at $0.10/$0.50, and grok-4.7 at $2.00/$6.00. Three of the four enter below the price of the model they sit above in their own generation ladder: Opus 5.5 is $1.00/$5.00 under Claude Opus 5, gpt-6-sol is exactly half of gpt-5.6-sol on both sides, and gpt-6-luna is half of gpt-5.6-luna on input and output alike. grok-4.7 enters at the same rate as grok-4.6, cache read included. This is price movement by new entry, not by repricing — no carried row moved, so a week-over-week delta computed on the carried set alone shows zero change while the cheapest way to buy a frontier-tier model got cheaper. The two are recorded separately here on purpose. Claude Opus 5.5 also carries a cache-read multiplier of 0.05x base input rather than the standard 0.1x, which the Anthropic page states explicitly; only Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 (0.025x) are cheaper on cache reads relative to their own input price. Newly observed and outside the rows: Google lists Gemini Omni Flash (gemini-omni-1.1-flash) and Gemini Omni Flash Preview, both at $1.50 input with output $9.00 for text and $17.50 for video, and describes them as a video generation and editing model billed at 5,792 tokens per second of 720p video — a video model, so outside a text-model series, on the same footing as the image, embedding, TTS, live and transcription lines already excluded. Google also lists Gemma 4, whose paid tier reads "Not available" across every category, so there is no paid API rate to record. Still observed and still out of the rows, unchanged from 2026-09-21: Mistral's two third-party GLM resales (GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.2, both $1.40/$4.40), excluded per the 2026-09-21 decision that a third-party model resold on a tracked provider's API is out of scope; Ministral 3 in three sizes (3B $0.10/$0.10, 8B $0.15/$0.15, 14B $0.20/$0.20); OpenAI's cyber line (gpt-5.6-cyber and gpt-5.5-cyber, both $12.50/$75.00, cached input $1.25) with the aliases gpt-daybreak-blue-latest and gpt-daybreak-red-latest pointing at gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-cyber; OpenAI gpt-5.2 and earlier; and Google's image, embedding, TTS, video, live and transcription models. Carried statements unchanged this week: Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer the page says produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text, with the exact increase depending on content and workload shape — per-token prices are unchanged, so the nine affected rows (claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, claude-mythos-5, claude-mythos-5-1) cost more per unit of text than a per-token comparison against a 4.6-and-earlier row shows; DeepSeek still accepts the legacy ids deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp while serving both from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at Flash pricing; the three Gemini Flash rows at $0.75/$3.75 still carry a 2026-12-31 introductory expiry that doubles them on 2027-01-01; Anthropic still states the Claude Sonnet 5 $2/$10 rate is standard and that the cancelled 2026-09-01 increase will not occur; and OpenAI still states gpt-5.6-sol's promotional pricing is available at least through 2026-11-21.
